steps.title: A varietal wine
steps.body: Made alone, Petit Verdot gives intense, dark wines with violet, blueberry, liquorice and spice, firm tannin and bright acidity. It can be austere young. Warm regions give rounder, riper styles. In Virginia, it has become a signature grape, ripening well in humid summers thanks to loose bunches that resist rot.

steps.title: Handling it
steps.body: Winemakers often pick it late for full ripeness, use gentle extraction to avoid harshness, and age it in oak to soften tannins. Some blend in a little Cabernet or Shiraz to round it out. Its high acidity helps it age, and good examples develop for a decade or more.

steps.prompt: Match each region to its Petit Verdot role.
steps.explanation: Petit Verdot plays different roles in different places.

steps.body: If you find a varietal Petit Verdot, decant it. Its tannins open up with air, and the violet aromas become clearer.

steps.prompt: Why does Petit Verdot handle Virginia's humid summers?
options: Thick skins and loose bunches resist rot
steps.explanation: Loose bunches let air circulate, reducing rot in humid conditions.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Varietal Petit Verdot is intense, floral and firm
Ripe picking, gentle extraction and oak soften it
Virginia, Australia and Spain make notable examples
